property.name: Roubený ráj
property.tagline: Libošovice · the southern tip of Bohemian Paradise
property.headline: Close the gate behind you and Bohemian Paradise is all yours
property.perex: A log cottage in Libošovice for nine guests plus an extra bed. Table tennis and table football in the barn, a table in the granary the rain can't reach, and a fire pit in the yard. The Plakánek valley starts on foot; Kost Castle is three kilometres away.
property.about: Roubený ráj stands in Libošovice, three kilometres from Sobotka, on the southern edge of Bohemian Paradise. It is rented whole — no other guests, no shared hallways, just your own party. The ground floor holds a cloakroom for rucksacks and wet boots, a bathroom, and a kitchen you can happily cook in for ten people at once. The attic hides three bedrooms, nine beds and an extra bed; the mattresses are orthopaedic on sprung slatted frames, so after a whole day on the rocks you really do sleep. In the evening you light the wood-burning stove, even though turning the thermostat of the central heating would do. And once the weather is good, life moves out into the yard anyway — to the fire pit, the barn and the granary.

beds.title: Nine beds and an extra bed
beds.description: Three attic bedrooms — two doubles and one sleeping five. Orthopaedic mattresses on sprung frames; in the morning only your calves will ache.

barn.title: A barn with ping-pong and table football
barn.description: Bats, balls and little men on rods. First a tournament "just for a minute", then a rematch that runs until dark.

granary.title: A granary instead of a pergola
granary.description: A table under old beams, out of reach of rain and midday sun. The evening ends when you decide it does.

fire.title: Fire pit and grill in the yard
fire.description: Grass underfoot, garden furniture, and a fire that is good to be quiet around. Bring your own sausages.

kitchen.title: A kitchen for the whole party
kitchen.description: Induction hob with an oven, dishwasher, microwave, toaster, kettle and fridge. It cooks for ten without complaining.

bathrooms.title: Two bathrooms
bathrooms.description: One downstairs, one in the attic — no morning queue. A washing machine goes without saying.

village.title: Shop and pub on foot
village.description: A grocery with a café a hundred metres away, a restaurant two hundred, the bus stop eighty. The car can stay parked all week.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi, and otherwise silence
wifi.description: The connection works if it has to. Most people stop looking for it after the first evening.

checkInOut.title: Self check-in and check-out
checkInOut.description:
A relaxed start to your stay, handled by self check-in.
No waiting for the keys to be handed over, no fitting your arrival around someone else's schedule. We send you everything you need before you set off, and you simply let yourselves in.

plakanek.title: Plakánek valley
plakanek.description: A sandstone gorge with a brook, ponds and old mills. Step out of the gate and you are soon walking under the cliffs straight to Kost Castle.

vesec.title: Vesec u Sobotky
vesec.description: A protected village reservation — a score of log houses together, as if the nineteenth century had stopped here.

kost.title: Kost Castle
kost.description: One of the best-preserved Gothic castles in Bohemia, set in a valley instead of on a hill. Tours, a torture chamber and birds of prey in season.

humprecht.title: Humprecht Chateau
humprecht.description: A Baroque hunting lodge above Sobotka. The oval hall has acoustics people still sing in today.

trosky.title: Trosky
trosky.description: Two towers, Baba and Panna, on the necks of extinct volcanoes. The emblem of Bohemian Paradise, recognisable even from the motorway.

hrubaSkala.title: Hrubá Skála
hrubaSkala.description: A rock town with viewpoints above the treetops and a chateau perched on a sandstone spur.

prachovskeSkaly.title: Prachov Rocks
prachovskeSkaly.description: The most famous rock maze of Bohemian Paradise. Ladders, ravines and lookouts that take in half the region.

jicin.title: Jičín
jicin.description: The town of Rumcajs and Wallenstein. A square, cake shops and museums — the perfect plan B for a rainy day.

checkInOut.question: When are check-in and check-out?
checkInOut.answer: Arrival from 15:00, departure by 10:00. We are happy to agree on another time.

howToBook.question: How does booking work?
howToBook.answer: You send a non-binding enquiry with your dates and the number of guests. Within 24 hours we confirm availability and the exact price. Only then are the dates firmly yours.

cancellation.question: Can I cancel?
cancellation.answer: Free cancellation up to 30 days before arrival. After that the deposit is refunded as agreed.

winter.question: Is the cottage suitable in winter?
winter.answer: Yes. It is heated by electric central heating, so the thermostat is all you need, and there is a wood-burning stove in the living area on top of that. The cottage is reachable by car in winter too, and you park right by the house.

rain.question: What is there to do when it rains?
rain.answer: The barn holds a ping-pong table and table football, and the granary has a covered table to sit at — the rain will not follow you there. And if it is set in for the whole day, Kost Castle and Jičín are both close by.

bikes.question: Where do we put our bikes?
bikes.answer: Bikes and scooters can be stored and locked up under a roof. There are two parking spaces right by the house and a further car park twenty metres away.

pets.question: Can we bring a dog?
pets.answer: Unfortunately not — pets are not allowed in the cottage. Thank you for understanding.

gallery.kitchen: Kitchen corner with a seating area
gallery.diningArea: Common room with the dining table
gallery.livingRoom: The parlour with the wood stove

novakovi.author: The Novák family
novakovi.text: This is our third year coming here. The owners are welcoming, the cottage still looks brand new, and there is no getting the kids out of the barn.

petr.author: Petr S.
petr.text: We came for a long weekend with friends. The kitchen can cook for eight, and we stretched the evenings out in the granary. Warmly recommended.

marketaJan.author: Markéta and Jan
marketaJan.text: You walk straight out of the gate into Plakánek and an hour later you are standing below Kost. Quiet, no neighbours, no car needed.

dvorakovi.author: The Dvořák family
dvorakovi.text: It rained three days out of four and nobody minded — the ping-pong tournament now has a sequel at home.

surroundings.heading: Plakánek begins at the gate
surroundings.perex: You do not need to drive anywhere. Step out of the gate, turn into the Plakánek valley and follow the sandstone gorge past the brook and the ponds all the way below Kost Castle. By car, Trosky, Hrubá Skála and the Prachov Rocks are within easy reach — and if you would rather stay put, the village has a shop with a café and a pub.
